name: The Spinanes
label: Merge
lede: One guitar, one drum kit, and a Portland duo that gave Sub Pop its first No. 1 on college radio before losing its drummer to Built to Spill.

eras.title: Two people at the IPU
eras.text: Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf made a full band's worth of noise with a guitar and a drum kit. Their first stage was the most important indie-rock gathering of 1991, K Records' week-long convention in Olympia.

years.h: Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf form the Spinanes in Portland
years.p: Singer-guitarist Rebecca Gates and drummer Scott Plouf start a two-piece in Portland, Oregon: no bass player, ever, in the original band.

years.cap: Olympia, August 1991: the Spinanes' live debut
years.h: The Spinanes debut at the International Pop Underground Convention
years.p: Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf play their first show at K Records' International Pop Underground Convention in Olympia, Washington. Their song Jad Fair Drives Women Wild lands on the IPU compilation.
years.xp: The song is named for [[Jad Fair|be4a8e65-a7ba-474c-989b-ed16e51c1a39]] of [[Half Japanese|18dc6bd7-9caa-4c2d-a2fc-e9546ebda6a4]]. The IPU compilation came out on K Records in 1991.

years.h: Two Spinanes singles on IMP Records
years.p: The Spinanes release two singles on the small IMP label. Merge later gathers the early sides as Imp Years.

eras.title: Sub Pop's college-radio No. 1
eras.text: Sub Pop was still selling grunge when it signed a Portland duo with no bass player. The Spinanes' first album went to the top of the college charts and put Noel, Jonah and Me on MTV's 120 Minutes.

years.h: Sub Pop signs the Spinanes and issues Spitfire
years.p: Sub Pop signs Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf and puts out the single Spitfire.

years.h: Manos: Sub Pop's first No. 1 on college radio
years.p: The Spinanes' debut album Manos becomes the first Sub Pop album to top the American college radio charts. Newsday's Ira Robbins rates it the ninth best album of 1993.
years.xp: Not everyone bought in: Robert Christgau called it a dud. Pitchfork later gave it 8.5, and the Chicago Tribune three stars.

years.h: Noel, Jonah and Me on MTV's 120 Minutes
years.p: The Spinanes' Noel, Jonah and Me gets heavy college and alternative airplay and a spot on MTV's 120 Minutes. A video for Sunday follows.

years.h: Stupid Crazy on Kill Rock Stars' Rock Stars Kill
years.p: The Spinanes contribute Stupid Crazy to Kill Rock Stars' compilation Rock Stars Kill.

eras.title: The drummer goes to Built to Spill
eras.text: The second album was the Spinanes' most ambitious as a duo. It was also the last: Scott Plouf had started drumming for Boise's Built to Spill, and Built to Spill had a major-label deal.

years.h: Strand, the Spinanes' second Sub Pop album
years.p: Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf's second album, Strand, is bookended by the singles Madding and Lines and Lines.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Spinanes · Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: Scott Plouf starts drumming for Built to Spill
years.p: Scott Plouf begins playing with [[Doug Martsch|42c520b5-4992-4aab-9f3f-542addcde686]]'s [[Built to Spill|3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0]], by then on Warner Bros., while still in the Spinanes.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Spinanes · Wikipedia: Built to Spill · AllMusic
years.h: Scott Plouf leaves the Spinanes for Built to Spill
years.p: After the Strand tour, Scott Plouf quits the Spinanes to drum full-time for [[Built to Spill|3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0]], the year of Perfect from Now On. He stays until 2012.
years.xp: Wikipedia ties the decision to Built to Spill's Warner Bros. contract. Plouf drummed on Keep It Like a Secret, Ancient Melodies of the Future, You in Reverse and There Is No Enemy.

eras.title: Chicago, Tortoise and a last record
eras.text: Rebecca Gates left Portland for Chicago and rebuilt the band as a trio, pulling in players from the city's post-rock scene. The result was the best-reviewed Spinanes album, and the end of the name.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Spinanes · Wikipedia: Arches and Aisles
years.h: Rebecca Gates rebuilds the Spinanes with Joanna Bolme and Jerry Busher
years.p: Now in Chicago, Rebecca Gates makes the Spinanes a trio with bassist [[Joanna Bolme|21f4bc79-8b24-4aee-85b3-22f46cf2e5d2]] and drummer [[Jerry Busher|59c39d46-efd2-4fa0-912e-93ead7a4ab97]].
years.xp: Bolme went on to play bass in [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]]'s Jicks and in [[Quasi|3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b]]. Busher spent years filling out [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]]'s live sound on drums, percussion and trumpet, and later formed [[French Toast|f9e0402f-c675-46d9-985f-07001bba6480]] with James Canty.

years.h: Arches and Aisles, with John McEntire and Sam Prekop
years.p: Recorded at Easley McCain in Memphis and at [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]]'s Soma studio in Chicago, with McEntire of [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]] co-producing and [[Sam Prekop|33175dbe-db6c-4f0b-a4c6-9addcd403186]] of [[The Sea and Cake|74171cb6-1ff8-42bd-be8a-96660c22e3e0]] singing.
years.xp: AllMusic called it the group's least confining, most listenable record; Trouser Press called it a superlative album of quietly remarkable songs. Pitchfork put it at No. 46 on its 2016 list of the best Pacific Northwest indie rock albums.

years.h: Imp Years: Merge collects the early singles
years.p: Merge Records gathers the Spinanes' early singles on Imp Years, the band's first release on Merge.

years.h: Rebecca Gates retires the Spinanes name for Ruby Series
years.p: Rebecca Gates ends the Spinanes and releases her solo debut, Ruby Series.

eras.title: Rediscovered on Merge
eras.text: Rebecca Gates kept making music and art, curating sound installations in Marfa and editing an audio arts magazine. Then Merge went back to the beginning and reissued the record that started it all.

years.p: Rebecca Gates' second solo album, The Float, features players from [[Quasi|3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b]], [[Wild Flag|4473e47b-81bb-47af-8cb0-1cad6f68d8bc]] and [[The Decemberists|97b1142f-c71e-4971-8736-4a8ceaf6b4c3]].

years.h: Merge reissues Manos as a lost '90s classic
years.p: Merge Records reissues the Spinanes' 1993 debut Manos. Vogue interviews Rebecca Gates about a lost '90s indie rock classic getting its deluxe edition.
